newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude firms, other grades hold value.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude firms, other grades hold value.

text.p: Brent crude differentials firmed on Monday in a market partly driven by traders' forward paper positions but also backed by reasonably strong fundamentals, traders said.
An early August (4-6) Brent traded at a strong August +5 cents - up 10 cents from Friday's deal.

Traders argued that last week's August -5 cents deal was below market and Monday's deal closer to Brent's real value in August and predicted the grade will continue at a premium to August for the rest of the week.
Although a number of sweet North Sea crudes remained available in the first decade of next month, buyers with specific requirements found sellers difficult to budge.
The best offer for early August barrels in late talk on Monday was at August +10 cents and an offer of Aug -5 cents for an end July loader could not be confirmed.
An August 5-7 cargo of Oseberg moved at a strong dated Brent +30 cents, while two to three Forties cargoes were heard to have moved at Dated Brent +38 cents.
There was no news of deferrals of further July loading Forties cargoes following the two confirmed last week.
The deferals were as a result of production problems on the Nelson field.

There were no Brent cargoes in the chains on Monday and only one (August 6-8) loader due to turn wet on Tuesday. This cargo was heard offered by a trader at August +10 cents on Monday though it is still technically a 15-day cargo.

Outright Brent prices were barely changed on the day with September down some three cents at $18.09 a barrel on the IPE by 1720 GMT. Similarly, CFD and intermonth spreads bounced around during the day but ended hardly changed.
Brent Sept/Oct spread traded twice at -10 cents with late bids seen at this level.

On the CFD's this week's dates were talked wide apart at September +5/+15 cents. July 28-01 moved at Sept -5 cents but action concentrated mainly on the Aug 4-8 week which traded straight and as part of a roll at Sept -10 cents.
